The teaching skills are mostly very good. The teachers are interested in their topic and know what they are talking about. At the same time students have enough free-time to do other activities (friends, sport, personal project, travel, etc.), which is a very good thing in my opinion. In addition, the different topics taught (both core and optional) are quite broad and interesting, which allows each of us to choose what we think would be the best for us. Finally, the masters provided me with a new way to approach things (especially referencing) which I really appreciate. That said, I do not believe that the course improved my ability to learn independently. I would say it gave me novel ideas about research structure, but not more knowledge.
The positive aspect of my whole course was my data mining module whereas a lecturer stands out. He is knowledgeable and knows how to impart knowledge to us fellow students.
The course is very interesting.

The MSc computer room is an excellent resource. The conversion course covers a wide range of topics relevant to future employment. The teaching inwas excellent and has provided a really good foundation.

A negative aspect is. Although helpful, this shouldn't be a core module, but instead should be provided as seminars. The reason for this is that it reduces the amount of modules that someone can take (which would have been more relevant to the MSc) and also it shouldn't have an impact on the final grade since it is more about acquiring skills (presentation skills, organization of work) than knowledge related to the topic undertaken.

There were aspects of the course which could benefit from some polish. The schedule of assignments is badly arranged at the end of the spring term. Just when the dissertation is being considered and arranged the workload was too full to achieve as high a level of work in the assignments - it required handing in work that should have had more attention. Likewise the GSA had some very interesting lectures, but trying to fit the workshops in proved impossible. As a post grad student who will be attending through the summer it seems silly to rush to finish it in the spring term. I also feel that the workshops were often overlong for the points they tried to get across.

I found the project research module, unfocused, largely irrelevant and pointless, and overly time consuming. I felt it consisted largely of GCSE level study gimmicks, which I found insulting. I also found the. I would not take another study course at the University of Kent because of my experience. I paid a lot of money for the course and I expect a better service for that money. In my opinion, the two tutors in question need to be reminded that they are not teaching raw undergraduates and to at least show a modicum of respect to that fact. If the amount of work and hassle that those two modules cause is considered reasonable then I would suggest that the rest of the course is unbalanced as I was not prepared for the effort required for those said modules.
Higher-level teaching content. Some of the course contents were not in-depth enough for a masters-level course. More details should be provided and concepts explored in greater depth.

The course contents have not been what I expected. It needs massive revision and scrutiny. Overall, I am not happy at all with this course at Kent and I regret coming here. It is not a university that I will recommend to others unless massive short comings are addressed. The lecturers especiallyneed to be changed.

For two particular seminars, my seminar leader wasn't as good as I was expecting. Not because they didn't know the subject but because they weren't explaining the task properly so it was quite confusing some times.

I thought that the course would have adequately prepared me for the dissertation that is to be completed. It did not. Since the dissertation is in the zenith of the programme, my programme should adequately equip me with the skills to do it and not merely complete it but at a high level. Most of the projects are programming based and a high level is expected, thus I believe more could have been done to improve students, especially those who did programming in term one. I would suggest that in term two for about half the term, the remainder of thetopics be covered. Mini projects within that same time frame should be given to mature us for the project dissertation.

Teaching assistants were not helpful and the course content was not helpful foras indicated in the website. The deliverables stated in the website to be obtained at the end of the course were not actualized. So we ended up without those skills and materials.
I wanted to focus mainly on programming but the course incorporates other things too.
The structure of my course is excellent and I feel the help they provide for all the students is fantastic.
Very good teaching. I am always looking forward to lectures and seminars.

A large part of the course feels dumbed down, and many subjects lack interesting depth. I often feel like I am surrounded by, and group work is an absolute nightmare. There is a distinct lack of dedicated Computing facilities when compared with other courses. There is a lot of repetition between modules, and some inconsistent overlap can be confusing. Overall, I feel disappointed in a large portion of the course.
